concepts.name: Response and predictor variables
concepts.summary: Identify which variable is being explained (response) and which are used to explain it (predictors) in a given question.

concepts.name: Scatterplot and association
concepts.summary: Read a scatterplot to describe direction, form and strength of the relationship between two quantitative variables.

concepts.name: Correlation coefficient
concepts.summary: Explain what r measures, its range from -1 to 1, and that it captures only linear association.

concepts.name: Line of best fit
concepts.summary: Understand that a straight line summarises how the response changes on average with the predictor.

concepts.name: Slope and intercept meaning
concepts.summary: Interpret the slope as the average change in response per one-unit increase in predictor and the intercept as the predicted value at zero.

concepts.name: Predicted values and residuals
concepts.summary: Describe a prediction as a point on the line and a residual as the observed value minus the predicted value.

misconceptions.text: A strong correlation proves that changes in the predictor cause changes in the response.
A correlation near zero means the two variables are unrelated.
The intercept always has a meaningful real-world interpretation.

concepts.name: Least squares estimation
concepts.summary: Explain that the fitted line minimises the sum of squared residuals and compute slope and intercept from summary statistics.

concepts.name: Making predictions from a fit
concepts.summary: Use a fitted equation to predict the response for new predictor values and avoid extrapolating beyond the data range.

concepts.name: Coefficient of determination
concepts.summary: Compute and interpret R² as the proportion of response variability explained by the model.

concepts.name: Residual plots
concepts.summary: Plot residuals against fitted values and spot curvature or changing spread that signals a poor linear fit.

concepts.name: Multiple regression with categorical predictors
concepts.summary: Encode a categorical predictor as indicator variables and interpret its coefficient relative to the reference group.

concepts.name: Outliers and influential points
concepts.summary: Recognise how an extreme point can pull the fitted line and check its effect by refitting without it.

misconceptions.text: A high R² means the model is correct and its predictions are reliable.
The regression line can safely be used to predict at any predictor value.
Outliers should always be deleted because they are errors.

concepts.name: Multiple linear regression model
concepts.summary: Fit a model with several predictors and interpret each coefficient as the effect holding the other predictors fixed.

concepts.name: Inference on coefficients
concepts.summary: Use standard errors, t-tests and confidence intervals to judge whether a coefficient differs from zero and how precisely it is estimated.

concepts.name: Overall F-test and adjusted R²
concepts.summary: Test whether the predictors jointly explain the response and compare models of different size using adjusted R².

concepts.name: Linear model assumptions diagnostics
concepts.summary: Assess linearity, independence, constant variance and normality of errors using residual plots and Q-Q plots.

concepts.name: Interaction terms
concepts.summary: Include and interpret an interaction so that the effect of one predictor depends on the level of another.

concepts.name: Multicollinearity
concepts.summary: Detect correlated predictors with VIF and explain how they inflate standard errors and destabilise coefficients.

concepts.name: Logistic regression and odds
concepts.summary: Model a binary outcome with the logit link and interpret exponentiated coefficients as odds ratios.

concepts.name: Transforming variables
concepts.summary: Apply log or polynomial transformations to fix nonlinearity or skew and interpret the resulting coefficients.

misconceptions.text: The response variable itself must be normally distributed for linear regression to be valid.
A non-significant coefficient proves that the predictor has no effect.
An odds ratio of 2 means the probability of the outcome doubles.

concepts.name: Model selection criteria
concepts.summary: Compare candidate models using AIC, BIC and subject knowledge and justify the choice while recognising selection bias.

concepts.name: Cross-validation for prediction
concepts.summary: Estimate predictive error on held-out data to judge generalisation and detect overfitting.

concepts.name: Regularisation methods
concepts.summary: Analyse how ridge and lasso penalties trade bias for variance and when each helps with many or correlated predictors.

concepts.name: Influence diagnostics
concepts.summary: Use leverage, studentised residuals and Cook's distance to separate outliers from points that change conclusions.

concepts.name: Heteroscedasticity and robust errors
concepts.summary: Diagnose non-constant variance and choose between transformation, weighting or robust standard errors.

concepts.name: Logistic model evaluation
concepts.summary: Evaluate a logistic model through discrimination, calibration and threshold-dependent metrics suited to the problem.

concepts.name: Generalised linear models
concepts.summary: Relate response distribution, link function and linear predictor to select models for counts, proportions and binary data.

concepts.name: Confounding and causal interpretation
concepts.summary: Judge when adjusted coefficients can be read causally and how omitted variables or colliders bias estimates.

misconceptions.text: Stepwise selection reliably finds the true set of predictors and its p-values remain valid.
Accuracy on the training data shows how well the model will predict new data.
Controlling for more variables always moves the estimate closer to the causal effect.

concepts.name: Bias-variance trade-off in modelling
concepts.summary: Evaluate how model complexity, sample size and regularisation shape error, and choose a strategy accordingly.

concepts.name: Hierarchical and mixed models
concepts.summary: Design models with random effects for clustered or repeated data and justify partial pooling over ignoring the structure.

concepts.name: Bayesian regression
concepts.summary: Specify priors, interpret posterior and predictive distributions and assess sensitivity to prior choices.

concepts.name: Flexible nonlinear regression
concepts.summary: Build models with splines or additive terms to capture nonlinear effects while controlling smoothness.

concepts.name: Causal inference with regression
concepts.summary: Design analyses using DAGs, instruments or quasi-experimental designs and defend the identifying assumptions.

concepts.name: Missing data and measurement error
concepts.summary: Assess how missingness mechanisms and noisy predictors bias estimates and select appropriate corrections.

concepts.name: Time series and dependent errors
concepts.summary: Detect serial or spatial correlation in residuals and apply generalised least squares or other models that handle it.

concepts.name: Reproducible modelling workflow
concepts.summary: Create an end-to-end analysis plan covering pre-specification, validation, uncertainty reporting and communication of limitations.

misconceptions.text: Mixed models are only a fancier way to get smaller p-values and can be replaced by adding group dummies without consequence.
Multiple imputation or complete-case analysis gives unbiased results regardless of why data are missing.
A flexible model with enough terms to fit the data closely is the best choice for inference.
